chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

In the description of The Eternal: He is One, Besought, One in meaning, not in multiple divergent meanings. He said: I said: May I be your ransom, a group from the people of Iraq claim that He hears with other than that which He sees by, and He sees with other than that which He hears by. He said: They have lied, deviated and likened (Allah to His creation) - Far elevated is Allah from that. He is Hearing, Seeing. He hears with what He sees by and sees with what He hears by. I said: They claim that He sees using that which they understand. He said: Elevated is Allah. Only that which has the attribute of the created can be understood and Allah is not like that.
ai.seo_question: How does the Imam describe the unity of Allah's attributes of hearing and seeing?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia doctrine of divine simplicity (Basit al-Jinan), asserting that Allah's attributes are identical to His essence rather than being distinct entities. The Imam refutes the Iraqi school's view of separate faculties for hearing and seeing, emphasizing that human intellect projects created, composite attributes onto the Creator, who transcends such limitations.
